newsitem.title: USA: Rep. Gonzalez calls on Fed to improve accounting.
newsitem.headline: Rep. Gonzalez calls on Fed to improve accounting.

text.p: Rep. Henry Gonzalez, a ranking Democrat on the House Banking Committee, on Monday called on the Federal Reserve to improve its system for counting cash at its branches around the nation.

Commenting on a draft report from the General Accounting Office on the San Francisco Fed's Los Angeles branch, Gonzalez (D-Texas) said in a statement, "The problems at the L.A. branch warrant immediate attention."
"Furthermore, he added, "the concerns of the GAO about other Federal Reserve cash facilities heighten the seriousness of the problems uncovered."
At Gonzalez's request, the GAO in June began investigating errors made in cash reports prepared by the Fed's L.A. branch.
The GAO was critical of the Los Angeles branch in its draft report and expressed concerns that problems at that bank might be occurring at other Fed banks as well.

"The L.A. bank's inability to precisely summarize currency activity from its cash inventory records raises serious questions about the integrity of its accounting and internal controls," the GAO said.
The agency urged the Fed to take steps to ensure that similar problems were not occurring at its other branches.
For its part, the Fed Board in Washington said it had conducted its own audit of the situation and found sound accounting practices at the Los Angeles branch.

"The examiners found that the accounting for cash handled by the branch was accurate and that proper safeguards and controls exist to ensure the integrity of the branch's financial records," the Fed said in a statement.
A Fed spokesman said the audit, part of a general review undertaken annually, was conducted between in late July and early August and was "significantly more comprehensive" than the GAO review.

Officials at the San Francisco Fed have confirmed that there were errors in some of its cash reports but have said the reports were statistical in nature and that the mistakes did not affect the financial position of the bank.
"We are confident of the integrity of the cash and financial situation of the bank," said Sandra Conlan, spokeswoman for the San Francisco Fed.
The GAO said it expects to release its final report on the Los Angeles branch around Sept. 30.
